commits.summary: example-targets: pipeline.py collect counted kqpykqpp's 19 applied jobs right, and now prints the totals itself (review item 8)
commits.body:
Review item 8 asked whether pipeline.py collect miscounted when kqpykqpp's commit message said outputs were applied for 18 jobs, though 19 receipts arrived. It didn't. Each of the 23 results' collected.applied lists 4 files for 19 jobs and none for the four preservation jobs of 285, 286, 287 and 306, which declare no output. collect printed one line per job and no total, and the collecting agent's sum of those lines was off by one. So there was no pipeline bug to reproduce.

To make a repeat less likely, collect's suggested commit message now opens with totals taken from the same lists (collect_totals): outputs applied for N of the M jobs, how many declared or produced none, how many were kept because the job didn't pass, and how many had conflicts. The new test test_collect_counts_the_jobs_whose_outputs_it_applied_for_the_commit_message failed before the change. The run-verification skill's collect step says to quote the totals.

Also read: item 7's job 20261115-054311-example-307-replay-its-receipt-records-b passed (collected in wtkxwrzk). 307's new replay receipt records before's BCrypt.class 0b137406... in spring-security-crypto 5.2.0.M4 (8871c1fe...) under claim.target.matched.
